name: containerize-aspnet-framework
description: Containerize an ASP.NET .NET Framework project for Windows containers.

Containerize the specified project, focusing **exclusively** on changes required to run it in a Windows Docker container. This is .NET Framework, not .NET Core. Use the settings supplied: project `.csproj`; Windows Server SKU (Core default or Full); version (2016/2019/2022); optional build/run base images; ports; run user (ContainerUser default); IIS settings; pre/post-build steps; GAC assemblies; MSIs; COM components; registry; environment variables; roles/features; files and destination; exclusions; `.dockerignore` additions; health endpoint/interval/timeout; other requirements and known issues. Unspecified settings use defaults.

✅ App configuration modification to ensure config builders are used to read app settings and connection strings from the environment variables
✅ Dockerfile creation and configuration for an ASP.NET application
✅ Specifying multiple stages in the Dockerfile to build/publish the application and copy the output to the final image
✅ Configuration of Windows container platform compatibility (Windows Server Core or Full)
✅ Proper handling of dependencies (GAC assemblies, MSIs, COM components)
❌ No infrastructure setup (assumed to be handled separately)
❌ No code changes beyond those required for containerization

1. Review settings; create `progress.md` with check marks.
2. Detect .NET Framework using `TargetFrameworkVersion` in the `.csproj`.
3. Select image matching framework, SKU, and Windows Server version. Tags: https://github.com/microsoft/dotnet-framework-docker/blob/main/README.aspnet.md#full-tag-listing
4. Required NuGet package: `Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment`. **DO NOT** install these if they are missing. If they are not installed, the user must install them manually. If they are not installed, pause executing this prompt and ask the user to install them using the Visual Studio NuGet Package Manager or Visual Studio package manager console.
5. Modify `web.config`: add ConfigBuilders section in configSections; add configBuilders in root; configure EnvironmentConfigBuilder for appSettings and connectionStrings:
`<section name="configBuilders" type="System.Configuration.ConfigurationBuildersSection, System.Configuration, Version=<REDACTED_IP>, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a" restartOnExternalChanges="false" requirePermission="false" />`
`<add name="Environment" type="Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.EnvironmentConfigBuilder, Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment" />`
Set `<appSettings configBuilders="Environment">` and `<connectionStrings configBuilders="Environment">`, retaining existing settings.
6. Create `LogMonitorConfig.json` beside Dockerfile, copying reference exactly unless settings require otherwise. Its contents **MUST NOT** not be modified and should match the reference content exactly unless instructions in containerization settings specify otherwise. Do not change issue logging level; Information for EventLog sources causes noise. Reference:
`"directory": "c:\\inetpub\\logs",`
`
